title: Friends
hook: friendship is a school of love
tomorrow: who prays for the people throwing the stones?

segments.voice: That was a week of people up close. A look that was already love. A fast with a washed face. One person, chosen again. A child in the middle of the room. Parents, honored honestly. And yesterday, Esau running down the road: brothers and sisters.
screen: `BROTHERS AND SISTERS.` → `A WEEK OF PEOPLE UP CLOSE.`

segments.voice: A teammate passes you the ball. A friend notices you haven't touched it all game, and asks why on the ride home. So what's the difference between a friend and a teammate? Jesus draws that line himself, the night before he dies, in John's Gospel. He tells his disciples he won't call them servants anymore, because a servant doesn't know what his master is doing. Then, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "But I have called you friends."
screen: `A TEAMMATE PASSES.` → `A FRIEND NOTICES.` → `I HAVE CALLED YOU FRIENDS.`

segments.voice: His reason is the surprise: friends, because everything he heard from his Father he has made known to them. A servant gets a task. A friend gets told what's going on inside. That's the line. Teammates share a goal; friends share what's real. And notice when he says it: not at a celebration, but at supper, hours before his arrest. He tells them they're friends right before the long night. Friendship isn't only for the good seasons. It's what holds when things go dark. A Cistercian abbot named Aelred of Rievaulx wrote a whole dialogue on spiritual friendship, and he opens it with a picture: here we are, you and I, and I hope a third, Christ, in the middle of us. That's why the tradition calls friendship a school of love. Look back at this week. Every lesson gets practiced on a friend first: full attention, choosing again after you let someone down, telling the truth kindly, running toward someone after a fight. Friends are where you rehearse it, and where you get it wrong safely enough to try again.
screen: `A SERVANT GETS A TASK.` · `A FRIEND GETS TOLD.` · `YOU AND I, AND A THIRD.` · then, large: `A SCHOOL OF LOVE.`

segments.voice: Count your friends on your fingers, slowly: the ones who know what's going on inside you, now or once. Give each finger a name and a second of thanks. When you reach the last one, pick one name you'd like to spend real time with soon, and start to plan it.
Friends. The ones you tell what's real, where love gets practiced first. Today's word.
Your line: a school of love. Jesus called them friends because he told them everything. One week of people, done.
